insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (Base Sum Insured and limits as per Policy Schedule; NCB up to 100%; ReAssure unlimited with per-claim cap up to Base Sum Insured)

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “The first paid claim triggers ReAssure, a benefit with unlimited sum insured. NOTE: Maximum amount ReAssure benefit pays for any single claim is up to base sum insured.”
great.explanation: After the first paid claim, ReAssure provides an unlimited additional sum insured for future claims in the same policy year. However, for any single claim it will pay only up to the base sum insured, so very large single hospitalizations may still be limited.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of a Pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases and their direct complications are not covered for the first 24 months from the policy start date. After 24 months of continuous coverage, PED-related claims become payable, which is market-standard.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of the listed conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first Policy.”
good.reference: Section 5.1(II) Specified disease/procedure waiting period (Code- Excl02)
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months from the policy start date. This is a standard waiting period and delays coverage for those conditions even if they are not pre-existing.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not covered in the first 30 days from policy commencement, but accidents are covered from day 1. This is the usual initial waiting period in retail health insurance.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.reference: Section 3.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days before hospitalization are covered if they relate to the same hospitalization. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.reference: Section 3.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)
good.explanation: Medical expenses incurred up to 180 days after discharge are covered if they relate to the same hospitalization. This supports longer recovery costs like follow-ups, diagnostics, and medicines.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “The default co-payment in the product is 50% which You can modify to 40% or 30% or 20% at inception of the first policy.”
bad.explanation: A co-pay applies on every admissible claim, with a default of 50% and options to reduce it to 40%/30%/20% only at first policy inception. This means you will always pay a large share of each claim out of pocket, which is a major drawback.

bad.name: Room Upgrade Co-pay
bad.quote: “You will have to bear additional 10% co-payment IF treatment is taken in higher room category than the eligible room category as specified in Your Policy Schedule”
bad.explanation: An additional 10% co-pay is charged if you take treatment in a higher room category than what your policy schedule allows. This can significantly increase your share of the bill if the eligible room category is restrictive.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Annexure I – The expenses that are not covered ... List I – Expenses not covered ... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 57 NEBULISATION KIT ... 68 VASOFIX SAFETY”
bad.reference: Annexure I – List I (Expenses not covered)
bad.explanation: Common hospital consumables like gloves, masks, nebulisation kits, and cannula-related items are not covered. These costs are frequently billed during hospitalization, so out-of-pocket expenses can add up.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: “We pay for Modern treatments as specified below: ... Robotic surgeries ... NOTE: A limit of maximum Rs. 1,00,000 per claim will apply to all robotic surgeries, except for total radical prostatectomy, cardiac surgeries, partial nephrectomy and surgeries for malignancies.”
bad.explanation: Modern treatments are covered, but most robotic surgeries are capped at Rs. 1,00,000 per claim (with some exceptions). If your robotic surgery costs more than this cap, you will have to pay the balance yourself.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: “All applicable benefits and details are mentioned in your Policy Schedule.”
unclear.explanation: The eligible room category/room rent limit is not stated in the wording and is only referenced as being in the Policy Schedule. Your actual room eligibility can materially affect claim payouts, so you must check the schedule to know the restriction.

unclear.name: No Claim Bonus
unclear.quote: “For every claim free year, we will add 10% of expiring policy base sum insured as NCB, maximum up to 100%.”
unclear.explanation: The sum insured increases by 10% of expiring base sum insured for each claim-free year, up to 100%. The wording here does not state what happens to the accumulated NCB after a claim (reduce or reset), so the impact on future cover is unclear.

unclear.name: Deductible
unclear.quote: “Annual Aggregate Deductible (optional benefit) ... This is an aggregate amount in a year ... which we will NOT pay.”
unclear.explanation: An optional annual aggregate deductible can be chosen, under which the insurer will not pay claims until the deductible amount is met in that year. The deductible amount is not specified in this extract, so you need the schedule/option details to know your out-of-pocket exposure.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
